title: The Balcony Harvest
subtitle: Growing Food in Small Spaces in Cool, Windy Climates
description_html:
Your balcony is windier, shadier and smaller than the gardening books assume. This one starts there.

Ines Halvorsen has grown salads, beans and strawberries on a west-facing seventh-floor balcony in Bergen for twelve years. In The Balcony Harvest she shows you how to:

  • read your balcony's sun, wind and shelter in one weekend
  • check lease rules and load limits before you buy a single container
  • build a windbreak that protects plants without turning your balcony into a wind tunnel
  • harvest salad every week from April to October
  • grow two or three summer crops that cope with cool nights

With 28 diagrams and photos, three real balconies followed through the year, and a month-by-month plan for cool climates from Montreal to Bergen.
